summary: The note covers the first week of Sam Bankman-Fried's fraud trial in Manhattan, where former MIT friends and FTX insiders Gary Wang and Adam Yedidia testified against him, along with Paradigm's Matt Huang. Wang, who pleaded guilty and is cooperating, described code giving Alameda unlimited withdrawals and a $65 billion line of credit, while Yedidia described flagging $8 billion in missing customer money. Ellison is expected to testify next as the prosecution's star witness.
one_line: Former FTX co-founder Gary Wang and engineer Adam Yedidia testified against Sam Bankman-Fried about code that let Alameda draw customer funds.
key_facts: Gary Wang, FTX's lesser-known co-founder and technology chief, told the court he committed financial crimes including wire and commodities fraud with Sam Bankman-Fried, Nishad Singh and Caroline Ellison.
Bankman-Fried faces seven federal charges, including wire fraud, securities fraud and money laundering, and the trial is set to last six weeks; Ellison is expected to testify Tuesday.
Wang testified that code in FTX's software gave Alameda unlimited withdrawals, negative balances and a $65 billion line of credit, resulting in Alameda owing FTX $8 billion in customer deposits.
Wang said the 'bug' was written by Nishad Singh, FTX's director of engineering, and reviewed by Wang, with Bankman-Fried 'calling the shots'.
In late 2021 Wang discovered Alameda had withdrawn $3 billion from its $65 billion line of credit.
Wang said an emergency meeting on shutting down Alameda ended without action because it had no way to repay a roughly $14 billion hole in its books.
Wang pleaded guilty in December, faces up to 50 years in prison, and signed a six-page cooperation agreement with prosecutors.
Wang owned 10% of Alameda and roughly 17% of FTX, with a base salary of $200,000 per year plus stock.

Adam Yedidia testified that in June 2022 he gave Bankman-Fried a Signal report showing $8 billion in customer money missing, and that Bankman-Fried said 'we were bulletproof last year. We aren't bulletproof this year.'
Yedidia earned a base salary of $175,000 to $200,000 plus bonuses of more than $12 million in cash and equity, mostly reinvested in FTX, and now teaches high school math.
Yedidia said Bankman-Fried assumed 'it's just Alameda paying for it' regarding rent on the $35 million Bahamas penthouse, home to a Signal thread called 'People of the House'.

Matt Huang of Paradigm testified the firm invested over $275 million in FTX, now wiped out, after Bankman-Fried assured him funds would not go to Alameda and that Alameda had no preferential treatment.
